title: Average Waiting Times at Polyclinics for Walk-in Patients and Plans to Redistribute Patient Load
what_it_is: Average Waiting Times at Polyclinics for Walk-in Patients and Plans to Redistribute Patient Load

sections.label: Walk-in consultation waiting times
sections.summary: In 2025 walk-in patients had median doctor consultation waiting time of eight minutes and 95th percentile of 72 minutes, with MOH not tracking peak versus off-peak.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In 2025, for walk-in patients, the median and 95th percentile doctor consultation waiting times were eight minutes and 72 minutes respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: However, the Ministry of Health (MOH) does not track waiting times by peak versus off-peak hours, but it is likely that 95th percentile waiting times happened during peak hours.

sections.label: Scheduled appointment waiting times
sections.summary: Scheduled appointments in 2025 had a median waiting time of about 10 minutes and a 95th percentile of up to 52 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: What we are trying to do is to stick as much as possible to more scheduled appointments, so, we minimise that variance as far as we can.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We see that for scheduled appointments, the median waiting time in 2025 for a scheduled appointment is about 10 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, you can see that the medical staff tries as far as they can to complete a consultation and conversation within an allocated timeframe so that they minimise the snowballing effect.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But the 95th percentile waiting time in 2025 for a scheduled appointment can go as high as 52 minutes.

sections.label: Walk-in versus scheduled appointments
sections.summary: The Ministry lacks numbers on walk-in versus scheduled appointment percentages, and cites CHAS GP clinics and Healthier SG for walk-in care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, over the longer term, does the Ministry have a datapoint for us to understand whether there are individuals who are making appointments or is that really going to be an extant problem that the healthcare system has to deal with and has to accept?

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I do not have the numbers for the percentage of walk-in versus scheduled appointments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But healthcare being the way it is, there will always be a sudden onset of discomfort and unwellness that will prompt a walk-in appointment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: That is why we do not work just based on polyclinic resources alone and we have resourced many of our general practitioner (GP) clinics with Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS), so that patients have an additional option to go to a nearby GP clinic and get subsidised treatment at the GP clinics as well, even if it is a walk-in situation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: It is about actually working with the entire resources of what we have in the entire healthcare ecosystem and not just focusing on polyclinics per se.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And I think, over time, as we improve on our Healthier SG enrolment, there will be better relationships between the patient and their enrolled GP so that that stronger nexus and better understanding between the patient and the GP will hopefully also spread the load out for each individual patient to the GP clinics where they also have easier access to care and nearer their homes as well.
